x: Two of them, in "Jerry" Thompson, a heavyweight Shot Putter whose best effort of 39ft. 1in. when he won the A.A.A. Handicap at Tooting, was very good; and Guy Hendry, who shows promise of becoming a really good high jumper, have already shown their worth.
Melchoir, Powell and Jerry Thompson were doing good work and bringing home the points. The Shot was won by the A.T.C., using the 12lb. shot.
Jerry Thompson will be our star in the Shot and Discus, assisted by Melchoir and Powell. On last season's showing it is hoped that Jerry may improve still more and reach 42 feet on occasions.

His best effort of the season was 163 ft. 10 ins. in the match at Gillingham. Jerry Thompson has lent valuable support with his good efforts with the Shot and Discus. His best performance was over 38 feet in the Shot.
We started off the present season with a serious handicap owing to Jerry Thompson, our best Shot Putter, having been confined to hospital suffering from sugar diabetes.

We welcome the return of Sid Jones and Bill Sutton from the Forces and genial Jerry Thompson, after suffering from sugar diabetes, has been one of the features of the Section's activities during the past summer.

Jerry Thompson beat Syd Jones in the Weight Putt, although both men have done better performances during the season. So concluded our first post-war championship meeting, and we have every reason to be more than satisfied with the various results.
